response: {"text":"This short overview is written for engineers or scientists from other areas who need a quick grasp of the key experimental observations and the main theoretical ideas behind heat‑driven electron release from solid surfaces. It starts with only basic undergraduate mathematics and builds a simple statistical‑mechanics picture, then derives several cornerstone formulas. One formula gives a universal link between temperature and emitted current for any material, another adds the influence of an external electric field, and a third adapts the universal relation to the case of a doped semiconductor using a specific model. Where necessary, brief quantum‑mechanical concepts are introduced, but no prior expertise in that field is assumed. The aim is to provide a concise, practical guide rather than an exhaustive encyclopedia."}
